intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the narrow lanes of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese street food including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee. Join a local-led walking tour or explore independently, stopping at tiny plastic-stool eateries and bustling market stalls that have fed locals for generations.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, a beautifully preserved trading port filled with colorful lanterns, centuries-old merchant houses, and tailors. Visit during the monthly Lantern Festival when electric lights are turned off and the town glows with candlelight. Sample Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from street vendors along the Thu Bon River.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a motorbike or join a budget group tour to ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, a dramatic mountain road stretching between Da Nang and Hue. The route offers breathtaking coastal views, misty peaks, and a raw sense of adventure that defines the backpacker trail through Central Vietnam. Stop at the old French and American war bunkers at the summit.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Boat & Village Tour
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, navigating narrow waterways by sampan boat through floating markets, rice paddies, and coconut candy workshops. Visit local villages in Ben Tre province, taste fresh tropical fruits, and witness the rural way of life that has remained unchanged for centuries.

experiences.name: Banh Mi & Pho Cooking Class in Ho Chi Minh City
experiences.description: Join an affordable hands-on cooking class in the backpacker-friendly Pham Ngu Lao district of Ho Chi Minh City. Learn to make authentic Vietnamese staples including Pho broth from scratch, fresh spring rolls, and the perfect Banh Mi assembly. Classes typically include a local market visit to source ingredients and a full meal at the end.
experiences.location: Pham Ngu Lao District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and arrange budget transport (grab taxi or airport shuttle) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Grab a quick late-night snack from a nearby 24-hour street stall if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On flight or airport terminal
meals.lunch: On flight or airport terminal
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near hotel upon arrival - look for banh mi or pho stalls open late (under $2 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Keep some Vietnamese Dong (VND) ready for transport and small purchases. Exchange money at the airport or use an ATM. Prioritize rest as Day 2 starts early.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up and explore the immediate beachfront area around Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a leisurely morning walk along the beach to get oriented. Visit the nearest local market to sample fresh tropical fruits and observe local vendors setting up stalls - a great cultural immersion experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town center by local xe om (motorbike taxi) or cheap local bus. Explore the main streets on foot, visiting any nearby pagodas or temples. Browse local shops and observe everyday Vietnamese life. Visit a local park or communal gathering space to watch locals play chess or badminton.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area and explore the local street food scene. Walk along the main food street and try various local snacks. Watch the sunset from the beach before heading to a budget-friendly local restaurant for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and banh mi from the local morning market (under $2 USD)
meals.lunch: Com tam (broken rice with grilled pork) from a local street stall ($1.50-$2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood BBQ at a beachside local eatery - grilled fish or squid with rice ($4-$6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Get a local SIM card today for cheap data and maps. Download Google Maps offline for the Vietnam region. Stay hydrated - April can be warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk on the beach. Join local fishermen returning from their morning catch at the nearby fishing pier - a wonderful authentic cultural experience. Practice bargaining at the morning wet market for fresh produce and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (budget $5-$8/day) to explore the surrounding countryside and nearby villages. Visit local rice paddies, small farming communities, and rural landscapes. Stop at any roadside Buddhist shrines or small pagodas for a cultural visit.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town and find a local cooking class or simply observe street food vendors preparing dishes. Spend the evening exploring the night market scene, trying various street snacks and chatting with other backpackers.

meals.breakfast: Pho bo (beef noodle soup) at a local pho stall ($1.50-$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Banh xeo (sizzling crepe) from a roadside vendor during countryside exploration ($1-$2 USD)
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread - try nem cuon (fresh spring rolls), grilled corn, and sugarcane juice ($3-$5 USD total)

day_by_day.notes: If renting a motorbike, ensure you have an international driving permit. Always wear a helmet. Negotiate rental prices before agreeing. Carry water and sunscreen for the afternoon ride.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the most prominent local cultural or historical landmark in the area - a communal house (dinh), old temple complex, or heritage site. Take time to read about the history and speak with local caretakers. Morning visits are less crowded and more atmospheric.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local handicraft scene. Visit workshops where artisans produce traditional Vietnamese crafts such as lacquerware, silk weaving, or bamboo products. Watch the craft process and purchase small inexpensive souvenirs directly from makers to support local economy.
day_by_day.evening: Join a street food walking tour (self-guided using a free blog guide or budget group tour around $5-$10 USD). Sample at least 5-6 different local dishes. End the evening with ca phe trung (egg coffee) or Vietnamese iced coffee at a local cafe.

meals.breakfast: Banh cuon (steamed rice rolls) with dipping sauce from a local stall ($1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Bun bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup) at a local noodle shop ($2-$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl - multiple small dishes including grilled skewers, fresh rolls, and local desserts ($4-$6 USD total)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting temples and pagodas - cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes before entering sacred spaces. A small donation to temple donation boxes is appreciated but not required.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to a nearby natural attraction - a waterfall, cave, national park trail, or scenic viewpoint accessible by local transport or rented bike. Pack a small picnic of street food snacks for the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the nature excursion and relax at the beach. Swim, read, or simply enjoy the scenery. Connect with other backpackers at the resort or nearby hostel common areas to exchange travel tips and recommendations.
day_by_day.evening: Attend any local cultural performance, community event, or traditional music show if available. Alternatively, find a rooftop bar or beachside spot for budget drinks (local Bia Hoi draft beer costs under $0.50 USD) and enjoy the evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a morning street cart ($1-$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed street food picnic - banh mi sandwiches and fruit bought from morning market ($2-$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant set menu or com binh dan (everyday Vietnamese rice plate) with multiple dishes ($3-$4 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Bia Hoi corners (street-side draft beer spots) are a quintessential Vietnamese backpacker experience. Look for plastic stools and low tables on street corners. Always drink bottled or filtered water - avoid tap water.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a deeper cultural experience - visit a local school, community center, or volunteer briefly with a local NGO if pre-arranged. Alternatively, attend a morning Buddhist ceremony at a local pagoda (typically 5-7 AM) for a peaceful and authentic experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local food culture more deeply. Visit a Vietnamese cooking supply market to see exotic ingredients, spices, and cooking tools. Take an affordable cooking class ($10-$15 USD) to learn how to make 2-3 classic Vietnamese dishes from a local home cook.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare and eat the dishes you cooked in the cooking class as your dinner. Spend the evening reviewing your travel photos, updating a travel journal, and planning the remaining days. Chat with fellow travelers at the hotel common area.

meals.breakfast: Chao (Vietnamese rice porridge/congee) with ginger and scallions from a street stall ($1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Light snacks and fresh coconut water while exploring the market ($1-$2 USD)
meals.dinner: Dishes prepared in your cooking class - typically pho, spring rolls, or a stir-fry ($10-$15 USD includes class fee)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes are excellent value and a great skill to take home. Look for classes hosted by local families rather than tourist-oriented businesses for more authentic instruction and better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longer day trip to a nearby town, village, or attraction requiring a 1-2 hour local bus or minivan ride. Visit a weekly local market if timing aligns - these rotating markets are incredible cultural experiences with ethnic minority vendors and unique regional products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the day trip destination. Visit any significant cultural sites, museums, or landmarks. Interact with locals and practice a few Vietnamese phrases - even basic greetings like 'xin chao' go a long way in building rapport.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Treat yourself to a budget-friendly Vietnamese massage ($8-$12 USD for a 60-minute traditional massage) to relax after a full week of exploring. End the day with a quiet beachside dinner.

meals.breakfast: Mi quang (turmeric noodles with pork and shrimp) at a local noodle house ($2 USD)
meals.lunch: Local specialty dish at the day trip destination - try whatever the region is known for ($2-$4 USD)
meals.dinner: Grilled fresh catch of the day at a beachside local restaurant with steamed rice and vegetables ($5-$7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: For day trips, confirm local bus schedules the evening before. Keep a note of the last bus return time to avoid being stranded. Carry small denomination VND bills for bus fares and market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning at the beach or local area doing something active - kayaking, snorkeling, or a beach volleyball game with other travelers. Many beach areas offer free or very cheap equipment rental through the resort or nearby vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit any remaining local sights you haven't yet explored. Seek out hidden gems recommended by locals or fellow backpackers - a secret viewpoint, a quiet fishing village, or a local family-run coffee plantation. These off-the-beaten-path spots are often the most memorable.
day_by_day.evening: Host or join an informal street food potluck with fellow backpackers - each person buys one street food item to share. This is a great social experience and very budget-friendly. Find a communal space on the beach or hotel common area.

meals.breakfast: Banh mi op la (banh mi with fried egg) from a street cart ($1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Hu tieu (southern-style noodle soup) at a local eatery ($2-$2.50 USD)
meals.dinner: Street food potluck with fellow travelers - budget $3-$5 USD for your contribution

day_by_day.notes: This is a good day to do laundry at a local laundromat (budget $1-$2 USD per kg) and repack your bag. Check if you need to book any onward transport and do so today to secure budget prices.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a meaningful cultural activity - visit a local museum, war memorial, or heritage exhibition to learn about Vietnamese history and the resilience of its people. This provides important context for everything you've observed during the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon doing final souvenir shopping at local markets rather than tourist shops. Look for handmade items, local spices, Vietnamese coffee, and silk products. Practice bargaining respectfully - start at 50-60% of the asking price and settle around 70-80%.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer-than-usual dinner at a mid-range local restaurant to celebrate your last full evening (budget $8-$12 USD). Try a dish you haven't yet sampled during the trip. Reflect on your favorite experiences over a final Vietnamese coffee.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese breakfast spread at a local cafe - pho, fresh juice, and coffee ($3-$4 USD)
meals.lunch: Bun cha (grilled pork with noodles) at a bustling local lunch spot ($2-$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at a well-reviewed local restaurant - try bo luc lac (shaking beef) or a regional specialty ($8-$12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: When bargaining, always remain friendly and smile. If a price seems too low, the vendor may be offended - aim for fair prices that work for both parties. Buying multiple items from one vendor often yields better discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach for one last peaceful moment. Pack your bags and do a final room check. Exchange any remaining large VND notes back to your home currency or keep small amounts as souvenirs. Write postcards to send home from the local post office.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final leisurely lunch at your favorite street food spot discovered during the trip. Take a final stroll through the local neighborhood, revisiting any favorite spots. Check out of the hotel and arrange budget transport to the airport or next destination.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Vietnam with incredible memories, new friendships, a fuller understanding of Vietnamese culture, and a stomach full of amazing food. Review your trip expenses and celebrate staying within budget.

meals.breakfast: One last bowl of pho at your favorite local stall - a perfect farewell meal ($1.50-$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Final banh mi and fresh coconut water from a street vendor ($2 USD)
meals.dinner: Airport terminal food or pack street snacks for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the airport at least 2-3 hours before international departure. Keep essential documents (passport, boarding pass, travel insurance) in your carry-on. Total estimated daily budget for this trip: $20-$35 USD per day including accommodation, food, transport, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect baggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort facilities.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport lounge
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport lounge
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a 24-hour convenience store or hotel room service upon arrival — try instant pho or bánh mì if available near the airport

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night light. Confirm hotel transfer in advance. Exchange some USD to VND at the airport for small expenses. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the immediate coastal neighborhood, breathe in the sea air, and get your bearings. Visit a nearby local market if one is within walking distance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into the nearest town center for a cultural orientation walk. Visit a local pagoda or temple to soak in Vietnamese spiritual culture. Browse small local shops and pick up a detailed map or join a free walking tour if available in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the local night market or main street food strip near the resort. Sample street food stalls and soak in the atmosphere of Vietnamese evening life.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — fuel up properly after the long journey
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (everyday Vietnamese rice plate) restaurant in town — budget-friendly and authentic, around 50,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Night market street food crawl — try bún bò Huế, grilled corn, and fresh spring rolls from different vendors, spending around 100,000–150,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Take it easy today. Stay hydrated — Vietnamese heat and humidity can be intense. Download Google Translate with Vietnamese offline pack and Grab app for local transport.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise beach walk along the resort's beachfront. After breakfast, join or arrange a local motorbike or bicycle rental and explore the coastal road heading north or south of the resort — a quintessential backpacker experience in Vietnam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby fishing village to observe traditional Vietnamese coastal life. Watch fishermen sort their catch, see colorful basket boats (thuyền thúng), and interact with locals. If a local cooking class is available in the area, this is a great afternoon option.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a sit-down dinner at a mid-range seafood restaurant on the beach. Watch the sunset over the water with a cold Bia Hơi (fresh draft beer).

meals.breakfast: Bánh mì from a local street cart near the resort — a classic Vietnamese breakfast for about 20,000–35,000 VND
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a fishing village eatery — grilled fish, clams, and rice for around 120,000–180,000 VND
meals.dinner: Beachfront seafood restaurant — try tôm nướng (grilled prawns) and cá chiên (fried fish) with rice, around 200,000–300,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Rent motorbikes only if you are a confident rider and wear a helmet at all times. Negotiate rental prices — expect 100,000–150,000 VND per day for a scooter. Bicycles are a safer and scenic option.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the nearest UNESCO or culturally significant site accessible from your resort location (such as Hội An Ancient Town, Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary, or Huế Citadel depending on exact resort location). Depart early by local bus or arranged transport to make the most of the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the cultural site — walk ancient streets, visit museums, temples, and artisan workshops. In Hội An for example, visit the Japanese Covered Bridge, Phúc Kiến Assembly Hall, and browse the tailor shops and lantern markets.
day_by_day.evening: If in Hội An, experience the magical lantern-lit Ancient Town at night — release a lantern on the Thu Bồn River. Dine at a heritage restaurant before returning to the resort by arranged transport.

meals.breakfast: Quick street breakfast before departure — xôi (sticky rice) or bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) from a roadside vendor, around 30,000–50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Cao Lầu or White Rose dumplings at a local restaurant in the cultural town — authentic regional dishes for around 60,000–100,000 VND
meals.dinner: Traditional Vietnamese set dinner at a mid-range heritage restaurant — try a set menu for around 200,000–280,000 VND including soup, main, and dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book transport the day before. Entry fees for cultural sites range from 80,000–150,000 VND. Dress modestly for temple visits — cover shoulders and knees. Carry cash as many vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a Vietnamese cooking class — a highlight for food-loving backpackers. Many local operators offer morning market visits followed by hands-on cooking sessions where you learn to make pho, spring rolls, and local specialties.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the cooking class (which often includes lunch), head back to the resort for some downtime. Spend the afternoon at the beach — swim, relax, or try water sports like kayaking or snorkeling if offered by the resort or local operators.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the resort town's local bar street or waterfront promenade. Join other backpackers at a rooftop bar for sundowners, then head to a local eatery for a casual dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included in cooking class market tour — sample fruits and snacks at the local market
meals.lunch: Your own cooking class creations — a unique and memorable meal!
meals.dinner: Casual local restaurant dinner — bún chả (grilled pork with noodles) or phở bò (beef pho) for around 60,000–100,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically cost 300,000–600,000 VND and include market visit, instruction, and lunch — great value. Book in advance as spots fill quickly. Apply sunscreen generously for the beach afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip or join a local tour to explore nearby natural attractions — islands, caves, or lagoons depending on your resort's location. Options might include a snorkeling trip to nearby coral reefs or a boat ride through mangrove forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local craft village or artisan workshop — silk weaving, lantern making, pottery, or lacquerware depending on the region. Try your hand at a craft activity and purchase a handmade souvenir directly from the artisan.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area for a relaxed evening. Visit a local spa for a traditional Vietnamese massage (around 200,000–300,000 VND for 60 minutes) before a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café — cà phê trứng (egg coffee) or cà phê sữa đá (iced milk coffee) with bánh mì
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the boat or at a local eatery near the craft village — fresh spring rolls and noodle soup
meals.dinner: Mid-range Vietnamese restaurant — try bò lúc lắc (shaking beef) or cơm tấm (broken rice with pork) for around 120,000–180,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Boat trips typically cost 200,000–500,000 VND depending on duration and destination. Negotiate group rates if traveling with other backpackers from the resort. Bring waterproof bags for electronics on the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a deeper cultural immersion — visit a local Vietnamese school, community center, or volunteer briefly with a local NGO if arrangements can be made. Alternatively, visit a local museum covering the region's history and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local street food scene systematically — join a street food tour or self-guide using a food map. Target specific dishes: chè (sweet dessert soup), bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), and nem lụi (grilled pork skewers).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese performance if available locally — water puppet show, folk music (đờn ca tài tử), or a cultural dance performance. These are typically inexpensive and deeply memorable.

meals.breakfast: Local pho shop breakfast — a steaming bowl of phở bò or phở gà for 50,000–80,000 VND
meals.lunch: Street food tour lunch — graze across 4–5 different street stalls spending around 100,000–150,000 VND total
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner at a restaurant near the performance venue — try a regional specialty you haven't tried yet, around 150,000–200,000 VND

day_by_day.notes: Water puppet shows typically cost 100,000–200,000 VND. Book tickets in advance for evening performances. Street food tours run by locals cost around 300,000–500,000 VND and are excellent value for guided tastings.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day hiking or trekking excursion to nearby hills, national park, or scenic viewpoint. Vietnam's landscapes are stunning and even short hikes reveal incredible views. Hire a local guide for cultural context and safety on unfamiliar trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local farmer's market or organic farm if accessible. Learn about Vietnamese agriculture, try fresh tropical fruits, and pick up local snacks. Alternatively, spend the afternoon exploring a lesser-known neighborhood away from tourist areas.
day_by_day.evening: Host a 'street food dinner' evening — challenge yourself to eat entirely from street vendors, trying dishes you haven't had yet. Walk the local food streets and explore with curiosity.

meals.breakfast: Early energy breakfast before the hike — xôi xéo (sticky rice with mung bean) or bánh mì ốp la (bánh mì with fried egg) for 30,000–50,000 VND
meals.lunch: Post-hike meal at a local restaurant near the trailhead — com ga (chicken rice) or bún thịt nướng (grilled pork noodle salad) for 70,000–100,000 VND
meals.dinner: Street food crawl dinner — bánh tráng nướng (grilled rice paper), bắp nướng (grilled corn), and chè ba màu (three-color dessert drink) for around 80,000–120,000 VND total

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes and bring water and sunscreen for the hike. Local guides charge around 200,000–400,000 VND for half-day treks. April weather can be hot — start the hike early to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to souvenir shopping and supporting local artisans. Visit a local market or craft street and purchase meaningful gifts — hand-embroidered items, lacquerware, silk scarves, or locally produced coffee and spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely afternoon for final exploration — revisit your favorite spots, take photos, journal your trip, or simply relax at the beach one last time. Consider a final swim or sunset kayak session.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a farewell dinner at one of the best mid-range restaurants in the area. Celebrate the trip with a full Vietnamese feast — multiple dishes, local rice wine (rượu gạo), and a proper dessert.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast — Vietnamese-style with cà phê sữa đá and bánh mì or a local breakfast set
meals.lunch: Light lunch while shopping — grab bún bò (beef noodle soup) or bánh cuốn at a market stall for 50,000–80,000 VND
meals.dinner: Farewell feast at a reputable mid-range restaurant — order 4–5 shared dishes including gỏi cuốn, canh chua (sour soup), thịt kho (braised pork), and cơm trắng (steamed rice), around 300,000–450,000 VND per person

day_by_day.notes: Budget 500,000–1,000,000 VND for souvenirs. Vacuum-sealed Vietnamese coffee (Trung Nguyên or local brands) makes excellent gifts. Bargain politely at markets but be fair — these are local livelihoods. Pack souvenirs carefully to avoid customs issues.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise beach walk or a quiet meditation moment at the resort. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast and begin packing. Check out procedures at Aegean Bliss Resort — confirm checkout time the night before.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time, use remaining hours for a final local café visit, last-minute shopping, or a relaxed sit by the beach. Store luggage at the hotel if checkout is before your transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange airport transfer and depart for the airport with ample time. Reflect on 10 incredible days in Vietnam — the flavors, the culture, the people, and the adventures.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or a local café — savor that last cà phê sữa đá and bánh mì
meals.lunch: Light meal near the hotel or airport — keep it simple with a bowl of pho or a bánh mì for the road
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on the plane — pick up some Vietnamese snacks (bánh tráng, dried fruits, local chips) at the airport for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Settle all hotel bills the night before to avoid morning rush. Keep some VND for airport tips and last purchases — exchange remaining VND back to USD at the airport. Leave a review for local guides, restaurants, and the resort to support the community. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled – late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive on Flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort's beachfront lounge, and enjoy a late-night light snack prepared by the resort chef.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable – in transit
meals.lunch: Not applicable – in transit
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome snack platter at Aegean Bliss Resort – fresh tropical fruits, Vietnamese spring rolls, and herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in amenities and a turndown service upon arrival. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning – enjoy a premium breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Take a sunrise stroll along the private beach, followed by a 60-minute rejuvenating spa welcome treatment (Vietnamese herbal body wrap) at the resort spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided cultural orientation tour of the nearest coastal town. Explore local temples, pagodas, and traditional Vietnamese architecture with a private English-speaking guide. Visit a local artisan market to observe lacquerware and silk weaving crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private pier, followed by a curated fine-dining experience at the resort's signature restaurant featuring modern Vietnamese cuisine with fresh seafood caught locally.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort oceanfront restaurant – Vietnamese pho, bánh mì, tropical fruit platters, and freshly brewed Vietnamese egg coffee
meals.lunch: Private chef-prepared beachside lunch at the resort – grilled tiger prawns, green papaya salad, and coconut rice
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant – 5-course tasting menu featuring seared tuna with lemongrass, crab bisque, slow-braised pork belly, and mango sorbet dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the spa welcome treatment in advance. Confirm private cultural guide booking. This is an orientation and relaxation day to ease into the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Premium street food walking tour in the nearby town – guided by a local culinary expert. Sample authentic Vietnamese street delicacies including bánh xèo (sizzling pancakes), bún bò Huế (spicy beef noodle soup), and freshly made chè (sweet dessert soups) from renowned local vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Vietnamese cooking class held at a heritage villa. Learn to prepare three signature Vietnamese dishes using locally sourced ingredients. Includes a market visit to select fresh produce with the chef.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a private beachfront candlelit dinner under the stars – a bespoke dining experience arranged by the resort's culinary team featuring a live acoustic Vietnamese musician.

meals.breakfast: Street food tour breakfast – freshly made bánh mì sandwiches, Vietnamese iced coffee, and steamed bánh bao buns from top-rated local stalls
meals.lunch: Cooking class lunch – enjoy the dishes you prepared: fresh spring rolls, caramelized clay pot fish, and lemongrass chicken with jasmine rice
meals.dinner: Private beachfront candlelit dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort – whole grilled lobster, truffle-infused pho broth, Vietnamese crème caramel (bánh flan)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the street food tour. Notify the cooking class of any dietary restrictions in advance. The beachfront dinner requires a 48-hour reservation with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered speedboat excursion to a nearby island or bay. Snorkeling in crystal-clear waters, followed by a guided exploration of a secluded beach cove. Enjoy a premium picnic breakfast on the boat with freshly prepared Vietnamese sandwiches and tropical juices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby UNESCO-listed heritage site or historic fishing village. Explore with a private historian guide, learning about Vietnamese maritime culture and ancient trading routes. Browse premium local craft shops for authentic souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop dining experience at a luxury restaurant in the nearest city or town, known for panoramic views and elevated Vietnamese fusion cuisine. Followed by a curated night market stroll to experience authentic Vietnamese evening street culture.

meals.breakfast: On-boat premium picnic – Vietnamese bánh mì, tropical fruit skewers, freshly squeezed sugarcane juice, and Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a premium restaurant near the heritage site – steamed clams in lemongrass broth, grilled fish with turmeric and dill, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine-dining restaurant – Vietnamese-French fusion tasting menu: duck confit with tamarind glaze, sea bass in banana leaf, and pandan panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen and snorkeling gear (or rent premium gear via the resort). Confirm boat charter 24 hours in advance. Night market stroll is casual – bring small local currency for street snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Morning yoga and meditation session on the resort's beachfront deck led by a private instructor. Follow with a premium Vietnamese breakfast and a leisurely swim in the resort infinity pool overlooking the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cultural immersion experience – visit a local Vietnamese family home for a traditional tea ceremony and insight into Vietnamese daily life and customs. Tour nearby rice paddies or fishing ponds with a local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show or cultural performance at a nearby theater. Followed by dinner at one of the region's most acclaimed fine-dining establishments specializing in Central Vietnamese royal cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort infinity pool terrace – congee with century egg, steamed dim sum, Vietnamese coffee, and fresh papaya with lime
meals.lunch: Traditional Vietnamese family home – home-cooked regional specialties including braised pork with eggs, morning glory stir-fry, and steamed rice with pickled vegetables
meals.dinner: Royal Vietnamese cuisine restaurant – imperial-style multi-course dinner featuring lotus seed soup, five-spice duck, shrimp paste rice cakes, and sesame sweet rice dessert

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the cultural home visit with the tour operator – a small gift for the host family (fruit basket or local sweets) is a thoughtful gesture. Book water puppet show tickets in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby natural landmark – a national park, limestone karst landscape, or scenic river valley. Private guided hiking or kayaking experience through stunning Vietnamese natural scenery. Suitable for all fitness levels with premium gear provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the natural reserve or return to a scenic riverside town for a leisurely cycle tour through local villages, paddy fields, and ancient temples with a private cycling guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a premium couples or solo spa experience – Vietnamese hot stone massage and aromatherapy treatment. Followed by a relaxed dinner at the resort's beachside grill.

meals.breakfast: Packed premium resort breakfast box – croissants, hard-boiled eggs, tropical fruits, Vietnamese iced coffee, and energy bars for the day trip
meals.lunch: Riverside or jungle-side premium picnic lunch arranged by the tour operator – fresh Vietnamese wraps, grilled corn, and watermelon
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort beachside grill – wood-fired seafood platter, grilled vegetables with fish sauce glaze, and coconut ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Wear light breathable clothing and sturdy footwear for outdoor activities. Apply insect repellent for jungle or nature reserve visits. Spa booking should be made the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter or seaplane scenic flight over the Vietnamese coastline, bay, or rice terraces (subject to availability in the region). Alternatively, a premium sunrise hot air balloon ride over the local landscape for breathtaking aerial views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium Vietnamese silk or lacquerware workshop. Participate in a hands-on artisan experience – try your hand at silk weaving or lacquer painting under the guidance of a master craftsman. Purchase bespoke handcrafted items.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive chef's table experience at the resort – dine in the kitchen with the head chef, watching your multi-course meal prepared live. Paired with a curated selection of Vietnamese wines and craft cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Pre-flight early breakfast at resort – eggs benedict with Vietnamese pork belly, fresh juices, and Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Artisan workshop district – lunch at a charming boutique café serving premium Vietnamese set lunch: noodle salad with grilled pork, fresh herbs, and iced lychee tea
meals.dinner: Chef's table at Aegean Bliss Resort – 7-course bespoke tasting menu with wine pairing: amuse-bouche, Vietnamese ceviche, wagyu beef pho, and passion fruit soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter or balloon rides require advance booking and are weather-dependent. Confirm 48 hours prior. Chef's table experience requires minimum 72-hour reservation and is limited to small groups.

day_by_day.morning: Premium street food deep-dive tour in a different neighborhood or town – focus on lesser-known regional specialties. Sample bún thịt nướng (grilled pork vermicelli), bánh căn (mini rice pancakes), and local herbal drinks with a food journalist or culinary guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a historic Vietnamese museum or cultural heritage center to deepen understanding of Vietnamese history, art, and civilization. Private guided tour with an academic expert. Explore a nearby ancient citadel or colonial-era architecture district.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar experience at a luxury hotel in the nearest city – craft cocktails inspired by Vietnamese botanicals (lemongrass gin, tamarind rum). Followed by dinner at a Michelin-recommended Vietnamese restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Street food tour – regional breakfast specialties: steamed rice cakes with shrimp, pork congee, and Vietnamese iced tea
meals.lunch: Heritage district boutique restaurant – premium Vietnamese set menu: lotus stem salad, clay pot catfish, and banana blossom dessert
meals.dinner: Michelin-recommended restaurant – contemporary Vietnamese cuisine: wagyu beef bánh mì sliders, squid ink rice with crab, and durian mousse with salted caramel

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the street food tour and heritage district exploration. Rooftop bar may have a smart-casual dress code – check in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort – final beach day. Enjoy premium watersports (paddleboarding, jet skiing, or sailing) arranged by the resort. Alternatively, relax with a book on the private beach with butler service.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium souvenir and luxury shopping experience – visit curated boutiques for Vietnamese silk garments, premium lacquerware, handcrafted jewelry, and artisan coffee blends. Private shopping concierge available to assist.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's finest venue – a grand beachfront celebration dinner. Live traditional Vietnamese music performance, a bespoke cocktail hour, and a lavish multi-course farewell feast with the resort's executive chef.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – full Vietnamese and continental spread: pho, dim sum, tropical fruits, pastries, eggs to order, and premium Vietnamese coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside butler lunch service – premium mezze-style spread with fresh seafood, Vietnamese dipping sauces, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Farewell gala beachfront dinner – 8-course Vietnamese feast: chilled lobster bisque, charcoal-grilled whole fish, Wagyu beef with lemongrass, and a decadent Vietnamese dessert tower

day_by_day.notes: Arrange luggage packing assistance through the resort concierge. Confirm checkout time and departure transfer for Day 10. The farewell dinner is a highlight – dress elegantly.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the private beach. Light yoga or meditation session. Enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the resort, savoring the ocean views one final time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Late checkout (if available) or use of resort day facilities – spa, pool, or lounge. Final exploration of the resort grounds. Private luxury transfer to the airport arranged by the resort concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day premium Vietnamese journey filled with culture, cuisine, and coastal luxury.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – Vietnamese egg coffee, freshly baked pastries, tropical fruit bowl, and a farewell smoothie crafted by the resort's nutritionist
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge dining or a final light meal at the resort before transfer – Vietnamese summer rolls, pho broth, and fresh lychee juice
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Request a late checkout at least 48 hours in advance. Confirm airport transfer timing based on flight schedule. Carry all purchased artisan items and gifts carefully in carry-on luggage if fragile.
